plain_definition: The informal, closed-door three-way negotiation between the European Parliament, the Council of the EU, and the European Commission that reconciles their differing positions on a piece of EU legislation into a single agreed text, once the Parliament and the Council have each adopted their own negotiating position. A trilogue does not itself finish the legislative process -- the resulting compromise text still has to be formally adopted by both the Parliament and the Council -- but it is the stage at which most of the real negotiation over a Regulation's or Directive's final wording happens. The digital euro Regulation entered trilogue in July 2026, after the European Parliament's plenary adopted its negotiating position on 9 July 2026.
formal_definition: Trilogues are not defined in the EU Treaties themselves; they are an informal tripartite negotiation practice between the European Parliament, the Council of the EU and the European Commission, used to agree a single compromise text under the ordinary legislative procedure (Article 294 TFEU) ahead of each institution's own formal adoption.
